find: All electrical installation work in the UK must comply with BS 7671 (the IET Wiring Regulations), and qualified electricians are responsible for testing and certifying that the work is safe before a building is occupied.
replace: Electrical work must be carried out by competent people. BS 7671 (the IET Wiring Regulations) is a widely used standard for electrical installations.
note: F1: BS 7671 is non-statutory.

expect:
Description of work (up to 3 marks): installs, inspects and tests electrical services and equipment; runs cables and fits consumer units (fuse boards); wires sockets, switches and lighting circuits; may install specialist equipment such as security systems or fire alarms (one mark per distinct point, up to 3).
Safety regulation (1 mark): for example, must comply with BS 7671 (the IET Wiring Regulations) and certify that completed work is safe before the building is occupied. [4 marks total]
value:
Description of work (up to 3 marks): installs, inspects and tests electrical services and equipment; runs cables and fits consumer units (fuse boards); wires sockets, switches and lighting circuits; may install specialist equipment such as security systems or fire alarms (one mark per distinct point, up to 3).
Safety requirement (1 mark): for example, works competently and follows relevant safety requirements; BS 7671 is a widely used standard for electrical installations. [4 marks total]
note: F2: Correct the electrical-safety answer key.

expect: What must an electrician comply with when installing electrical services in a new building?
value: What widely used standard guides electrical installation work in a new building?
note: F3: Do not present BS 7671 as an unconditional legal requirement.

expect: BS 7671 (the IET Wiring Regulations), certifying work is safe before occupation.
value: BS 7671, the IET Wiring Regulations, is a widely used standard for electrical installations.
note: F3: State the standard accurately.

find: Sites must be securely fenced and clearly signed to prevent unauthorised access by members of the public, including children.
replace: Sites must take steps to prevent unauthorised public access, such as using secure fencing and clear signs.
note: F4: State the CDM duty without prescribing one measure for every site.

find: The primary piece of UK legislation governing workplace health and safety, placing duties on employers to protect the health, safety and welfare of their employees and others affected by their work.
replace: The main workplace health and safety law in Great Britain, placing duties on employers to protect the health, safety and welfare of their employees and others affected by their work.
note: F5: The Act does not extend to Northern Ireland.

find: is the cornerstone of workplace safety law in the UK.
replace: is the main workplace safety law in Great Britain.
note: F5: Correct the Act’s territorial scope.

expect: The primary piece of UK legislation governing workplace health and safety, placing duties on employers to protect the health, safety and welfare of their employees and others affected by their work.
value: The main workplace health and safety law in Great Britain, placing duties on employers to protect the health, safety and welfare of their employees and others affected by their work.
note: F5: The Northern Ireland equivalent is different legislation.

expect: Which of the following is the primary piece of UK legislation placing duties on employers to protect the health, safety and welfare of all employees and others in the workplace?
value: Which of the following is the main piece of legislation in Great Britain placing duties on employers to protect the health, safety and welfare of all employees and others in the workplace?
note: F5: Correct the Act’s territorial scope.

find: Under this Act, employers in construction are legally required to prepare risk assessments, decide what control measures are necessary, and prevent or control exposure to hazards. They must also ensure that the hierarchy of control is followed when selecting those measures, monitor the level of exposure to hazards over time, prepare accident procedures so that incidents are dealt with promptly and correctly, and provide adequate training and supervision to all employees so they can carry out their work safely.
replace: Health and safety regulations require employers in construction to prepare risk assessments, decide what control measures are necessary, and prevent or control exposure to hazards. They must also ensure that the hierarchy of control is followed when selecting those measures, monitor the level of exposure to hazards over time, prepare accident procedures so that incidents are dealt with promptly and correctly, and provide adequate training and supervision to all employees so they can carry out their work safely.
note: F6: Do not assign regulations’ explicit duties to the 1974 Act alone.

find: data-revision-tip="Learn the six employer duties under the Health and Safety at Work Act: risk assessments, control measures, preventing/controlling exposure, hierarchy of control, monitoring, accident procedures, training and supervision."
replace: data-revision-tip="Remember the seven employer duties under health and safety regulations: risk assessments, control measures, preventing/controlling exposure, hierarchy of control, monitoring, accident procedures, training and supervision."
note: F6: Correct both the legal attribution and the count.

find: Under the Health and Safety at Work Act, employers must: prepare risk assessments; decide on control measures; prevent or control exposure to hazards; follow the hierarchy of control; monitor exposure levels; have accident procedures in place; and train and supervise employees.
replace: Under health and safety regulations, employers must: prepare risk assessments; decide on control measures; prevent or control exposure to hazards; follow the hierarchy of control; monitor exposure levels; have accident procedures in place; and train and supervise employees.
note: F6: Keep the required duties but attribute them accurately.

find: The Health and Safety at Work Act requires employers to assess risks, implement control measures, monitor hazards, prepare accident procedures, and train and supervise workers.
replace: Health and safety regulations require employers to assess risks, implement control measures, monitor hazards, prepare accident procedures, and train and supervise workers.
note: F6: The listed duties are not all imposed by the Act alone.

expect: Describe the employer duties required by the Health and Safety at Work Act on a construction project.
value: Describe employer health and safety duties on a construction project.
note: F6: Do not misattribute the whole duty list to one Act.

expect: Name three employer duties under the Health and Safety at Work Act.
value: Name three employer duties under health and safety regulations.
note: F6: Do not misattribute the whole duty list to one Act.

find: For gas work, this means being registered with Gas Safe — it is illegal for an unregistered person to carry out any work on gas appliances or pipework.
replace: For gas work carried out as part of a business, this means being registered with Gas Safe — it is illegal for an unregistered person to carry out gas work on appliances or pipework.
note: F7: Preserve the business-work legal requirement without outlawing permitted user tasks.

expect: What accreditation must a person hold to legally carry out gas work in the UK?
value: What registration is required for someone carrying out gas work as part of a business?
note: F7: State the legal scope accurately.

find: For electrical installation, inspection and testing, the relevant accreditation scheme is NICEIC (the National Inspection Council for Electrical Installation Contracting), which provides evidence that the electrician is competent and their work meets required safety standards.
replace: NICEIC is one certification scheme for electrical businesses. Electrical work must be carried out by competent people and meet relevant safety requirements.
note: F8: NICEIC certifies businesses; it is not an accreditation every electrician must hold.

find: A person with the appropriate qualifications, training, experience and accreditations to safely carry out a specific type of work, such as a Gas Safe registered engineer or a NICEIC-approved electrician.
replace: A person with the training, experience and competence to safely carry out a specific type of work, such as a Gas Safe registered engineer.
note: F8: NICEIC certification applies to businesses rather than every individual electrician.

find: Gas work requires Gas Safe registration; electrical work requires NICEIC accreditation.
replace: Gas work done as part of a business requires Gas Safe registration; electrical work must be carried out by competent people.
note: F7/F8: Correct the gas-work scope and NICEIC claim.

find: For gas and electricity questions, always name the specific accreditation — Gas Safe for gas; NICEIC for electrical work — and always mention isolation before work begins.
replace: For gas and electricity questions, name the relevant safety requirement — Gas Safe for gas; a competent person and, where relevant, an electrical scheme such as NICEIC, for electrical work — and mention safe isolation before work begins.
note: F8/F9: NICEIC is one scheme, and isolation is normally the safe procedure.

expect:
Which one of the following is the correct accreditation scheme for an electrician carrying out installation work on a construction site?
A) Gas Safe
B) COSHH
C) NICEIC
D) CIOB
value:
Which one of the following is an electrical certification scheme?
A) Gas Safe
B) COSHH
C) NICEIC
D) CIOB
note: F8: NICEIC is a scheme, not a compulsory personal accreditation.

expect: An accreditation scheme confirming an electrician is competent and meets required safety standards.
value: A certification body that assesses electrical businesses against relevant safety standards.
note: F8: NICEIC assesses businesses, not every individual electrician.

expect: A person with the appropriate qualifications, training, experience and accreditations to safely carry out a specific type of work, such as a Gas Safe registered engineer or a NICEIC-approved electrician.
value: A person with the training, experience and competence to safely carry out a specific type of work, such as a Gas Safe registered engineer.
note: F8: NICEIC certification applies to businesses rather than every individual electrician.

find: The most important of these is isolation — knowing how to cut off the supply of gas, water or electricity before starting any work.
replace: A key safety procedure is isolation — knowing how to cut off the supply of gas, water or electricity before work, where it is safe and practicable to do so.
note: F9: Live electrical work is a tightly limited exception.

find: All services must be isolated before work begins, using lock-out/tag-out or valve isolation procedures.
replace: Services should normally be isolated before work begins, using lock-out/tag-out or valve isolation procedures.
note: F9: Live electrical work is a tightly limited exception.

expect:
A maintenance plumber is called to repair a gas boiler and a burst water pipe in the same property. Both jobs require working on live services.

Evaluate the safety steps the plumber must take for each job before and during the work, and explain why Gas Safe registration is particularly important for the gas work.
value:
A maintenance plumber is called to repair a gas boiler and a burst water pipe in the same property. Both jobs involve services that are live before work begins.

Evaluate the safety steps the plumber must take for each job before and during the work, and explain why Gas Safe registration is particularly important for the gas work.
note: F9: Do not imply that the repairs require live working.

expect: What must always be done to a gas, water or electricity supply before starting any work on that service?
value: What should normally be done to a gas, water or electricity supply before starting work on that service?
note: F9: Do not erase the limited legal exception for live electrical work.

find: An <dfn class="term" data-def="A space that is enclosed or partially enclosed, not designed for continuous human occupancy, and which has a foreseeable risk of serious injury due to hazardous substances, lack of oxygen or other dangerous conditions.">enclosed space</dfn> is any area that is fully or partially enclosed, not designed for people to work in on a regular basis, and where there is a foreseeable risk of serious injury or death.
replace: An <dfn class="term" data-def="A place that is enclosed or partially enclosed and has a foreseeable risk of serious injury from hazardous substances or dangerous conditions.">enclosed space</dfn> is a fully or partly enclosed place where there is a foreseeable risk of serious injury from hazardous substances or dangerous conditions.
note: F10: Use the risk-based legal definition.

expect: A space that is enclosed or partially enclosed, not designed for continuous human occupancy, and which has a foreseeable risk of serious injury due to hazardous substances, lack of oxygen or other dangerous conditions.
value: A place that is enclosed or partially enclosed and has a foreseeable risk of serious injury from hazardous substances or dangerous conditions.
note: F10: Use the risk-based legal definition.

find: On construction sites, enclosed spaces include manholes, culverts, storage tanks, sewers, ductwork and deep excavations.
replace: On construction sites, enclosed spaces may include manholes, culverts, storage tanks, sewers, ductwork and deep excavations where the relevant risks are present.
note: F11: A location is enclosed only when the relevant foreseeable risk exists.

find: Workers must use atmospheric monitoring equipment to test air quality before entering and while working, and must wear appropriate PPE such as breathing apparatus if oxygen levels or gas concentrations are hazardous.
replace: Where the risk assessment identifies an unsafe atmosphere, workers must test air quality before entry and monitor it during the work as needed. They may need breathing apparatus or other suitable PPE.
note: F12: Testing, monitoring and PPE follow the risk assessment.

find: This means a trained attendant must remain outside the space at all times, in communication with those inside, with the means to summon help and, if safe to do so, to extract an incapacitated worker.
replace: This usually includes a trained person outside the space who can raise the alarm and start the rescue plan.
note: F13: Do not turn one rescue arrangement into a universal legal rule.

find: Enclosed spaces carry risks of fumes, reduced oxygen, flooding, fire/explosion and entrapment; rescue arrangements — including a trained attendant outside — must be in place before entry.
replace: Enclosed spaces carry risks of fumes, reduced oxygen, flooding, fire/explosion and entrapment; suitable rescue arrangements must be in place before entry.
note: F13: Rescue arrangements must match the risk assessment.

find: For enclosed spaces, the most commonly missed point is the requirement for rescue arrangements — many students write about PPE but forget that a trained attendant and a rescue plan must be in place before anyone enters.
replace: For enclosed spaces, remember that suitable rescue arrangements must be in place before anyone enters.
note: F13: Keep the legal rescue duty without prescribing a universal attendant.

expect: Who must remain outside an enclosed space while workers are inside?
value: Who should be available to raise the alarm and start a rescue if needed?
note: F13: State the risk-based rescue role.

expect: A trained attendant, able to summon help and carry out rescue if needed.
value: A trained person who can raise the alarm and start the planned rescue.
note: F13: State the risk-based rescue role.
